attempts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: EIGHT-FRAME WALK CYCLE ANIMATION SPRITE SHEET, 4 columns × 2 rows, pure solid white background with no grid lines or text.
Input image 1 is the ONLY identity, art style and CAMERA DIRECTION reference. This is the northeast view: the lumberjack walks away toward the UPPER RIGHT of the screen, seen FROM BEHIND. His broad olive-green back is visible and his nose points upper-right, only a small right facial profile visible. Do not turn toward the viewer. No apron on the back.
Input image 2 is a motion reference ONLY: it shows alternating leg contacts in its two rows. Do not use its north-facing camera. Render all 8 figures with the exact northeast camera of image 1.
Create eight genuinely different successive frames of ONE natural IN-PLACE walking cycle. Chest and pelvis stay anchored at the same position relative to each equal cell. Same head size and body scale. Same orange cap, dark beard, olive tunic and cream rolled cuffs, brown pants and boots. Same axe gripped in ANATOMICAL RIGHT HAND through the entire cycle; the anatomical left hand is empty. Do not mirror the character or swap hands. Restrained opposite arm swing, axe stays safely low.
CRITICAL: The two rows must depict OPPOSITE halves of the stride, with visibly exchanged leading legs, not eight variations of the same pose.
Read frames left to right across top row then bottom row:
1. LEFT FOOT forward toward screen upper-right, RIGHT FOOT far backward toward lower-left. Left foot contacting, right heel raised. This is opposite to the leg ordering in reference image 1.
2. Weight settles onto LEFT FOOT; right knee bends, trailing right boot starting to lift, body slightly lower.
3. RIGHT swinging boot PASSES close beside planted LEFT ankle: feet close together, right knee raised, distinct narrow passing silhouette.
4. RIGHT boot swings forward upper-right with knee bent, left stance leg extends backward; body slightly raised, approaching opposite contact.
5. RIGHT FOOT far forward upper-right, LEFT FOOT far backward lower-left. This resembles the leg ordering of reference image 1 and is VISIBLY OPPOSITE to frame 1.
6. Weight settles onto RIGHT FOOT; left knee bends, trailing left boot starting to lift, body slightly lower.
7. LEFT swinging boot PASSES close beside planted RIGHT ankle: feet close together, left knee raised, distinct narrow passing silhouette.
8. LEFT boot swings forward upper-right with knee bent, right stance leg extends backward; body slightly raised, approaching frame1.
Keep an actual rhythmic walking gait, not shuffling. Do not repeat frame1 as frame8. Lock back-facing upper-right direction in EVERY cell. High elevated RTS painted illustration camera exactly like image1, readable cap top plane, no perspective zoom changes. Warm hand-painted material shading and crisp outlines of image1. Full body including all boot tips and entire axe in every cell; generous white gaps so no neighboring overlap. No carried log, no smoke, no labels, no motion trails. Compose eight equal-sized isolated sprites.
attempts.outcome: Correct northeast facing, right-hand axe and identity, but largely same left trailing/right leading leg ordering in both rows. Passing frames 3 and 7 differ; insufficient full alternating stride.

attempts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct ONLY THE LEGS in bottom-row figures 1, 2 and 4 of this 4-column by 2-row eight-frame lumberjack animation sheet. Keep all torso, heads, clothing style, right-hand axes, camera, framing, scale, background, and all four TOP ROW figures unchanged. Keep bottom row figure3's close passing legs unchanged.
The current error is that nearly every figure has his LEFT leg stretched BACKWARD to the lowest boot on the sheet and his RIGHT boot tucked forward high at the right. To make the missing opposite half of the walk cycle:
BOTTOM ROW FIGURE 1 (frame5): put the ANATOMICAL RIGHT LEG — the leg on the SAME SIDE AS THE AXE, emerging below the RIGHT hip — fully BACKWARD toward the lowest boot position at lower-left of the figure, extended with heel up and boot sole visible. Put the ANATOMICAL LEFT LEG — empty-hand side — FORWARD toward upper-right, foreshortened so its boot sits HIGHER behind the extended near right leg. The near right thigh must now cross IN FRONT OF the farther left thigh. This is the opposite stride from the top-left figure, while the TORSO still faces away upper-right.
BOTTOM ROW FIGURE 2 (frame6): keep the same OPPOSITE leg ordering as bottom figure1: RIGHT leg trails toward the lowest boot position, heel lifts and knee flexes; LEFT leg is planted forward high upper-right.
BOTTOM ROW FIGURE 4 (frame8): RIGHT leg supports backward, LEFT knee swings FORWARD upper-right approaching the next step; different from bottom figure1. Bring left boot up in front, not backward.
Anatomical RIGHT foot must visibly exchange its gait role with LEFT foot between top row and bottom row. The top row shows LEFT trailing/RIGHT forward. The bottom row needs RIGHT trailing/LEFT forward. Do not just redraw the same stride. Do not mirror the entire person, do not swap the axe hand, do not turn the body, and do not rotate camera. Pure WHITE background unchanged. This surgical animation correction changes only the three specified lower-body leg poses.
attempts.outcome: Targeted leg correction changes foot roll but does not visibly exchange the extended trailing leg. Rejected as ineffective motion correction.
